questions.question: Apply drama techniques to design an anti-drug campaign. / [CO2, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Apply drama techniques to design an anti-drug campaign [A] / [CO2, CO4]- 5 marks
  • a) Use street theatre or role-play to show the harmful effects of drug abuse on individuals and families.
  • b) Create strong characters and conflict that demonstrate the dangers of addiction and making healthy choices.
  • c) Include emotional storytelling to help the audience connect with the victims of drug abuse.
  • d) Encourage audience participation through interactive drama or discussion after the performance.
  • e) End with a clear message and solution, such as seeking help, counselling, or community support.

questions.question: Analyze the effectiveness of traditional media compared to digital media in rural development. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the effectiveness of traditional media compared to digital media in rural development -[An] / [CO1] -5 marks
  •  Traditional media (radio, folk media, street theatre) are accessible to rural populations with limited internet access.
  •  Digital media (social media, websites, mobile apps) allow faster communication and wider reach.
  •  Traditional media build stronger cultural connection and trust in rural communities.
  •  Digital media enable interactive communication and quick feedback.
  •  Combining both media types often produces the most effective rural development communication.

questions.solution_html:
• Apply visual hierarchy principles in designing a health awareness poster. [A] / [CO1-5 marks

questions.question: Explain the communication process with a neat diagram and examples. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the communication process with a neat diagram and examples [E] / [CO5] -10 marks
  • Communication Process- Communication is the process of sending and receiving messages between a sender and a
  • receiver to achieve mutual understanding.
  • Diagram of Communication Process
  • Sender → Encoding → Message → Channel → Receiver → Decoding → Feedback→ Noise
  • Important Points
  • a) Sender – the person who initiates the message.
  • b) Encoding – converting ideas into words, symbols, or gestures.
  • c) Message – the information or idea being communicated.
  • d) Channel – the medium used (speech, phone, radio, social media).
  • e) Receiver – the person who receives the message.
  • f) Decoding – interpreting the meaning of the message.
  • g) Feedback – response from the receiver confirming understanding.
  • h) Noise – barriers that distort communication (language problems, distractions).
  • i) Example: A health worker explaining vaccination benefits to villagers.
  • j) Effective communication occurs when the receiver clearly understands the message.

questions.question: Evaluate how communication skills determine the impact of policy writing outputs. / [CO3, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate how communication skills determine the impact of policy writing outputs. [E] / [CO3, CO5]- 10 marks
  • a) Clear language helps readers easily understand policy recommendations.
  • b) Logical structure and organization improve readability and comprehension.
  • c) Accurate data presentation increases credibility and trust.
  • d) Persuasive writing techniques help influence decision-makers and stakeholders.
  • e) Concise and focused content avoids confusion and improves effectiveness.
  • f) Use of visuals such as charts and graphs helps explain complex data.
  • g) Appropriate tone and professionalism strengthen the authority of the document.
  • h) Audience-focused writing ensures the policy addresses stakeholder needs.
  • i) Strong conclusions and recommendations guide policymakers toward action.
  • j) Effective communication skills ultimately increase the chances of policy adoption and implementation

questions.question: Evaluate ethical dilemmas in television and radio reporting. / [CO5] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate ethical dilemmas in television and radio reporting. [E] / [CO5]- 10 marks
  • a) Balancing truth and sensationalism while reporting news.
  • b) Protecting privacy of victims and vulnerable individuals.
  • c) Avoiding biased or misleading information in reporting.
  • d) Ensuring accuracy and fact-checking before broadcasting.
  • e) Managing conflicts of interest between journalists and organizations.
  • f) Responsible coverage of violence and disasters without causing panic.
  • g) Respecting cultural and social sensitivities in media content.
  • h) Avoiding manipulation or editing that distorts reality.
  • i) Maintaining independence from political or corporate pressure.
  • j) Following professional media ethics guidelines set by organizations like the Press Council of India.
